To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the relevant abstract representation for high-level planning in continuous environments is the set of all sets of states reachable by a sequence of high-level actions; (ii) the relevant abstract representations for high-level planning under uncertainty is a set of probability distributions over states, one for each high-level action; (iii) learning these representations is a specific instance of probabilistic density or classification estimation.
(1) abstract representations for high-level planning are sets of states and (2) abstract representations for probabilistic high-level planning are distributions over states.
